article_lead.description: the fraction of predictions with the right label, a quick performance summary that needs class-specific context

new_bank_questions.title: Accuracy under a prevalence shift
new_bank_questions.body: A fixed binary classifier has sensitivity 0.80 and specificity 0.90. What is its accuracy when the positive-class prevalence is 0.10? What is it when the prevalence is 0.50, assuming the class-specific rates stay fixed? Explain why the two accuracies differ.
new_bank_questions.answer: With prevalence π, accuracy = π·sensitivity + (1−π)·specificity. At prevalence 0.10 it is 0.10(0.80)+0.90(0.90)=0.89. At prevalence 0.50 it is 0.50(0.80)+0.50(0.90)=0.85. The classifier's conditional error rates are unchanged, but overall accuracy weights them by the class mix, which has changed.
